title: Use semantic boundaries for independently retrievable chunks

state.decision_rationale: Superseded by the narrower symbol-boundary experiment. Do not add external retrieval-unit identities until boundary quality, stability, and partial-retrieval workflows are demonstrated.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable critique 3: fixed chunking is content-blind
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Chunk on symbol boundaries, falling back to 64 lines only in outline-less files, so chunks are semantically coherent, independently citable, and reusable as retrieval units.
feedback.normalized_claim: Make reliable symbol boundaries the primary chunking signal, with bounded deterministic fallbacks, and evaluate resulting chunks as retrieval units.

current_behavior: Exact chunks use a fixed 64-line maximum and reconstruct source exactly.
The reported packet had 472 exactly-64-line chunks among 632 total, but that measurement was not independently reproduced.
Outlines may be unavailable, partial, nested, overlapping, or have unknown ranges, so symbol-only chunking needs explicit fallbacks and size caps.

proposal.summary: Evaluate symbol-coherent chunks as a stricter variant of boundary snapping, including direct retrieval-unit identifiers and exact reconstruction guarantees.
candidate_changes: Define deterministic partitioning for nested symbols, file-level preambles, gaps, overlapping ranges, and oversized symbols.
Retain a maximum-size fallback so a single huge symbol cannot monopolize a retrieval unit.
Give chunks stable packet-local addresses and preserve exact byte concatenation.
Benchmark retrieval quality against fixed chunks and the narrower near-boundary snapping proposal.
non_goals: Do not require analyzer success to include exact source.
Do not equate syntactic symbol coherence with optimal context for every task.
Do not discard comments, imports, or inter-symbol source gaps.

questions: Should chunks contain one top-level symbol, multiple small siblings, or target a size window?
How are headings, config sections, and non-code structure treated?
Are symbol-aware chunk IDs stable enough for external retrieval indexes?
risks: Analyzer churn can invalidate retrieval-unit boundaries and caches.
Semantic chunks can become highly uneven in size.
Retrieval may need cross-boundary context that the symbol partition hides.
evidence_needed: RAG retrieval evaluations using fixed, snapped, and symbol-primary chunks.
Exact round-trip and determinism tests across partial-outline cases.
